No new npm or cargo dependencies; bun.lock unchanged.
Strict TypeScript (no any, no @ts-ignore), Biome style, ASCII only, no emojis; cargo commands with CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true.

Editor legality checks only in Editor intent methods, never in applyCommands, command validation, History, clipboard, imports or collab.

Each worker edits only its writePaths, its declared sharedPaths with the fresh-read and pre/post sha256 protocol, and its own impl-plans/progress/<planId>.md; foreground commands only; format only own files.

designDecisionsAndRationale: BPMN elements are first-class registry types with semantic payloads (not styled shapes) so AI tools can read and diff semantics separately from visual data (design 3.2).
Waypoint-basis math moves from core connector.ts into @diagra/ir because @diagra/io needs it and cannot import @diagra/core (design 5.2).

One renderer-neutral notation module feeds both the SVG export and ui-solid views so canvas and export cannot diverge and tests can count roles; MarkerKind is unchanged because it keys Record tables (design 6.1, 6.2).

Connection legality lives in Editor intent methods (connectBpmn, connectSmart delegation, reconnectBpmnFlow, updateBpmnSemantic) so imports, undo, clipboard and collab keep accepting stored documents (design 4.3).
Hand-written non-validating XML parser and deterministic serializer that rejects DOCTYPE, avoiding dependencies (design 5.1, 14).
Export route resolver is injected through options.routeOf so io does not depend on core (design 5.3).
Lint rule semantics are ported from bpmnlint documentation and pinned by per-rule tests and reference rule-id multisets; messages use diagra's own wording (design 7.3, 13).
Cross-package fixture acceptance tests live in @diagra/core because only core dev-depends on @diagra/io (bpmn-13).

Test ownership (design 11.1): pinned-list tests registry.test.ts and golden.test.ts plus the new canonical __fixtures__/bpmn.jsonl belong to bpmn-01; bpmn-02 and bpmn-14 own bun tests so every plan reports a positive pass count.
User-QA defaults: lane delete cascades (Q1), desktop lint always uses recommended (Q2), SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 with no migration (Q3).
intentionalTradeoffs: Deleting a lane deletes its member nodes (cascade), unlike bpmn-js; undo restores them.
BPMNDI ids (<id>_di) and edge docking points are regenerated on export; semantic ids, shape/label bounds and interior waypoints are preserved.
Older builds reject documents containing a bpmn page with a value.enum error instead of a newer-schema message.
A top-edge lane resize is treated as a bottom-edge resize; a direct lane width change is restored from the parent (design 4.4).
keyBetween RangeError fallback in addBpmnLane can leave a lane above its members until reordered.
No palette entry for boundary events (Descriptive palette); they are created through import and the API.
Text summary line of lint output has no leading symbol.

packages/core/src/bpmn/index.ts is a designated shared barrel appended by bpmn-03/04/05 in wave 2 under the pre/post sha256 protocol; the orchestrator verifies all 6 expected export lines after wave 2 (reconciliation.afterWave2).
supportedEdgeCases: Nested lanes, collapsed black-box pools, expanded and collapsed sub-processes, boundary events (interrupting and non-interrupting).
Message flow inside one pool, sequence flow across pools, incoming flow to a start event and outgoing flow from an end event are rejected or corrected at edit time but accepted on import/undo/collab.
Unsupported BPMN constructs and foreign XML extension content preserved with import warnings, never silently dropped; DOCTYPE and malformed XML rejected with a parse error.
Reference-file tests skip when .reference is absent (CI) and run locally.
Imported .bpmn in the desktop stays detached (filePath null) so autosave never overwrites the source file.
Pool move translates lanes and contents; lane resize restacks siblings with one undo step.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Lane deletion that re-parents nodes instead of cascading
Per-document or desktop lint configuration; plugin:* extends (config error)
A pool placed over existing tasks uses generic nextIndex placement
